claim_ceiling: temporal evidence inclusion and replay semantics only

snapshot_semantics.as_known_at: Only events first received at or before receiver_receipt_watermark_unix_ms may influence the historical result.
snapshot_semantics.recomputed_with_current_trust: Reassess the same historical query using current trust/key status while retaining the original as_known_at result.
snapshot_semantics.issuer_recorded_at: Self-declared source metadata; not a receipt or trusted timestamp.
snapshot_semantics.trusted_timestamp: Must bind the canonical payload digest; does not prove event truth or effective time.

cases.purpose: A valid observation with no calibration events is accepted only at the binding-only ceiling.
A revocation is received before the snapshot but is not effective until after it.
Issuer claims early recording, but receiver first saw the event after the historical receipt watermark.
A revocation is received and effective before the requested snapshot.
The measurement clock interval overlaps the exclusive calibration end boundary.
The supplied timestamp token does not bind the event payload digest.
The signature is valid but authority to issue this certificate event is unknown.
The event is received but the owner-native sequence/checkpoint evidence shows a gap.
Two events reuse one source-scoped immutable ID with different payload digests; neither may win by array order.
The old snapshot accepted an event while its key was not known compromised; current reassessment lacks an independent timestamp proving pre-compromise existence.
Two corrections point to each other, so no unique historical event state exists.
The source event time regresses relative to a trusted owner sequence/receipt observation.
The source claims an early record time and a receiver first-seen time, but no verifiable receipt evidence or digest binding is supplied.
The same local event ID is used by two different source namespaces; composite source-namespace/event-ID identities remain distinct and both effective events are considered.
At-least-once delivery repeats the exact same source-scoped event and payload digest; the event is counted once, with duplicate receipt retained for audit.

A single issuer principal presents the same local event ID under a second unverified namespace. Namespace separation is accepted only when the binding from namespace to issuer is trusted; an unverified alias must not bypass duplicate-identity detection.
